videos.script: Joana asked where the Salesforce database runs. There is no answer she can use. {{platform}} Salesforce is one platform shared by many thousands of companies. Serra Alta rents a slice of it, called an org. It cannot connect to the database, choose when to upgrade, or run code without limits. {{limits}} This lesson is about what renting means for an architect. First, the platform itself: objects, fields, three releases a year, and the governor limits that keep one tenant from slowing the rest. {{clicks}} Then customisation. Fields, rules and Flow, before code, and the debt both leave behind. Serra Alta's Account object carries four hundred and twelve custom fields, and a third of them are empty. {{night}} Then the APIs, and one month-end night when an invoice sync used up the org's daily allowance, and the reps' orders stopped reaching SAP. {{owner}} And last, the question every company with a CRM and an ERP has to answer. Which system owns the customer? The answer turns out to be one field at a time.
